method: Site-specific HistGradientBoosting absolute-error ensembles predict demand and dwell time from local hour, weekday, charger limit and the optional last-request snapshot, using separate targets, two-seed averaging, recent-day weighting, request-value transforms and a charger-time demand cap. Arrival rates use weekday-by-96-slot empirical frequencies. The deterministic 15-minute world model retains five joint ExtraTrees demand/dwell quantile cohorts for future arrivals and represents each current vehicle with three joint ExtraTrees demand/dwell cohorts at probabilities 0.2, 0.6 and 0.2. Each current cohort keeps the demand and dwell predicted by the same tree, is centered on the survival-adjusted remaining dwell, and preserves expected vehicle count and remaining energy. Historical quarter-hour arrival counts are aligned from the current local step for any supplied window length and normalized by same-weekday training coverage. Future-arrival intensity is additionally conditioned on the current parked-vehicle count using site-and-origin regressions fitted only from complete training days. Vehicles whose predicted dwell has elapsed use a training-only conditional survival residual. The model simulates every fractional current and future cohort under both natural and capacity_edf interventions from the same state; capacity_edf uses complete earliest-predicted-departure ordering without an arbitrary service-vehicle budget. Completion-aware dispatch applies a 1.25 demand-planning margin, caps the optional request snapshot at 1.35 times predicted demand, protects vehicles with no deadline slack, and concentrates scarce capacity on the smallest jobs. Office1 uses slack-first scheduling and shares residual power with tail-uncertainty vehicles whose predicted demand is satisfied but whose observed completion is still pending.
assumptions: Only current-step observations are used for online actions.
Recent historical sessions are more representative of future behavior.
last_requested_energy_kwh is an optional snapshot and is never treated as a known final target.
Request uncertainty is bounded by the documented 1.35 demand-shift factor.
Demand, dwell and arrival assumptions stay unchanged when only counterfactual capacity changes.
Every charging interval is 0.25 hours and future charger capacity is 6.6 kW.
Historical arrivals are aggregate same-weekday counts aligned to the current quarter-hour step.
Current parked-vehicle count is available online and is predictive of future arrival intensity.
limitations: Vehicle demand and departure time remain uncertain at arrival.
Office1 has sparse history, so its site-specific estimate is less stable.
capacity_edf represents a simulated physical response rather than real user behavior.
The model cannot read hidden truth or future arrivals and may fail under distribution shift.
